initiative.name: Gombe Goes Green (3G) Carbon Sequestration Initiative
initiative.description: The Gombe Goes Green (3G) initiative is a major environmental project launched by the Gombe State Government in Nigeria in 2019. It has successfully planted 5 million trees across 11 Local Government Areas to combat land degradation, soil erosion, and the advancing Sahara Desert. The project focuses on five key areas: large-scale afforestation (e.g., Kanawa Forest Reserve), agroforestry for farmers, urban forestry, forest protection via an MRV framework, and decentralized nurseries that employ youth and women. Seeking registration under the BioCarbon Standard, the project follows the BCR0001-ARR methodology for a 20-year crediting period (2026–2045). With a 70%–85% tree survival rate, it expects to sequester 1.05M to 2.13M tCO2e, valued between $7.35M and $21.25M. The initiative creates green jobs, boosts food security through windbreaks, empowers women, and restores biodiversity. Technical partners include Onyx Investment Advisory, ACReSAL, and FRIN.
initiative.participants: Gombe State Government and Onyx Investment Advisory Ltd

The Puerto Zábalo and Los Monos REDD+ project aims to contribute to the sustainable development of its communities while preserving the existing forests in the territory of the Reserve. initiative.name: CRIMA Predio Putumayo y Andoque de Aduche REDD+ Project
initiative.holder_name: REGIONAL INDIGENA DEL MEDIO AMAZONAS (REGIONAL INDIGENOUS COUNCIL OF THE MIDDLE AMAZON) – CRIMA
initiative.description:
The CRIMA Predio Putumayo y Andoque de Aduche REDD+ Project seeks the conservation of
forests located in the indigenous territories of Andoque de Aduche Indigenous Reserve, in the
municipality of Solano in the department of Caquetá; and in the areas of the indigenous
communities of Puerto Zábalo y Los Monos, and Monochoa zone that are part of the Great Predio
Putumayo Indigenous Reserve in the municipalities of Puerto Santander, Puerto Alegría and La
Chorrera in the department of Amazonas. The project area has a total area of 1,436,973 ha at the
beginning of the monitoring period. The project aims to contribute to mitigate the effects caused
by climate change by reducing 50,757,609 tCO2e emissions derived from deforestation and forest
degradation during the 40-year crediting period, which is equivalent to an average emission
reduction of 1,268,940 tCO2e/year.

initiative.name: Proyecto de Mitigación Forestal Resguardo Indígena TICOYA
initiative.description: The Tikuna, Cocama, and Yagua Indigenous Reserve Forest Mitigation Project (TICOYA) is a local initiative of the Association of Indigenous Authorities ATICOYA. The project seeks the certification of actions related to the reduction of carbon emissions due to unplanned deforestation in around 131,531.7 ha of dense forests belonging to the TICOYA Indigenous Reserve, located in the municipalities of Puerto Nariño and Leticia (Amazonas). The Project expects the reduction of 2,263,951 tCO2e through the implementation of activities related to five strategic lines, recovery, and rehabilitation of forests; sustainable agricultural production and business projects; strengthening of food security through traditional production systems (chagras), monitoring, and strengthening of governance.
initiative.participants: Resguardo Indígena Tikuna, Cocama y Yagua (TICOYA), South Pole Carbon Asset Management S.A.S

initiative.name: Project for Forestry Restoration in Productive and Biological Corridors in the Eastern Plains of Colombia
initiative.description: The Project for Forestry Restoration in Productive and Biological Corridors in the Eastern Plains of Colombia has as its objective to employ the international carbon market as a key incentive for investments in new commercial forest plantations and restoration of natural forests in the remote High Orinoco region of Colombia. initiative.name: PARAMUNO Project 1
initiative.description: Paramuno is a climate change mitigation project targeting the reduction of greenhouse gases through the conservation of forests and paramos in the Colombian Andes. It addresses the degradation of high-mountain ecosystems caused by increased water and resource demand, climate change, tourism, mining, and agricultural expansion. The project supports sustainable transitions in these ecosystems, providing economic incentives for conservation and strengthening local governance. A primary strategy is selling carbon credits to combat deforestation and land-use change. Project Paramuno P1 also aims to support Sustainable Development Goals 6, 13, and 15, targeting clean water, climate action, and life on land. It aspires to achieve the Orchid category, signifying its commitment to long-term social and environmental benefits.

initiative.name: Proyecto de Conservación Delfines Cupica REDD+
initiative.holder_name: Consejo Comunitario General Los Delfines, Consejo Comunitario de Cupica y Biofix Consultoría S.A.S BIC.
initiative.description: The DELFINES CUPICA Conservation Project seeks the conservation of the forests located in recognition of the Afro-Colombian communities grouped in the two Community Councils that integrate and propose this project. The specific objectives of the DELFINES CUPICA REDD+ Conservation Project are: to mitigate the effects caused by climate change through the implementation of measures for the reduction and capturing of CO2 emissions, by avoiding deforestation and promoting the restoration of degraded forest territories. To promote the sustainable management of the forests located in the area of influence of the project by forest custodians, by encouraging productive activities well-suited with the reduction of emissions generated by deforestation. To cooperate in the conservation of biodiversity by protecting the ecological connectivity and habitat of those species that are included in a threatened category and those that represent an ecological interest due to their capacity to adapt to climate change, such as sea turtles and mangroves. To contribute to gender equity education by increasing the capacity for leadership, participation, empowerment and entrepreneurship of women within the Community Councils.
initiative.participants: Consejo Comunitario General Los Delfines, Consejo Comunitario de Cupica y BIOFIX BIC Consultoría S.A.S BIC.
initiative.localitation: The area covered by the project is 113,025 hectares and is located in the properties of the collective territories awarded to the Consejos Comunitarios General Costa Pacífica Norte del Chocó "Los Delfines" y de Cupica.
